content: Hello, I wanted to share that I've built an open-source CLI tool that allows you to connect your Codex/Claude Code/Gemini or local models and start autoformalizing from .tex - https://github.com/ulamai/ulamai This is an early version, but already works for math olympiads and got used in a formalization of an Erdos problem (small part): https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/thread/433 I'm happy to help anyone set it up, and of course would love to get your feedback on what to add/fix. Plus if you have any suggestions on where to direct it at to be useful to mathlib, would love that too!
@Przemek Chojecki This looks exciting to be vendor independent. How mature is the system? How does it compare to LSP-MSP or other dedicated provers?

Bas Spitters said:

Przemek Chojecki This looks exciting to be vendor independent. How mature is the system? How does it compare to LSP-MSP or other dedicated provers?

UlamAI is an early but functional system: it already runs end-to-end Lean workflows (prove + TeX formalize), supports multiple LLM backends, has resume/artifact pipelines, deterministic replay scaffolding, regression tests, and increasingly strict anti-cheat semantic checks (including locked-proof resume guards). So it is usable for iterative formalization work today, but still in fast-moving v0.1.x territory rather than a fully hardened research-grade prover stack.

Compared to dedicated provers like LSP-MSP-class systems, Ulam currently prioritizes practical CLI integration, Lean validation loops, and engineering ergonomics over peak theorem-proving performance. Those dedicated systems typically have stronger learned policies/value models, more mature search optimization, and benchmark-tuned training pipelines. Ulam is closer to a robust, extensible proving/formalization platform-in- progress; it is not yet state-of-the-art on formal prover benchmarks, but it is moving in that direction with v0.2 goals (better state canonicalization, scoring, retrieval, and stronger search controls).
What do you think about the possibility of lean-lsp MCP instead of the dojo? (MCP has goal state)

I don't have a preference here, it's definitely doable to add it next to Dojo as a choice for a backend (we'd have then LeanDojo, plain Lean, and Lean-LSP). Added it to the pipeline, at some point it's worth benchmarking that - thank you for the suggestion. Also this is what GPT 5.2 gave me for comparison:

  • lean-lsp via MCP is better for UX and robustness: easier setup, fewer Pantograph/toolchain mismatch failures, direct goal/diagnostic access in normal Lean workflow.
  • Dojo is still better for strict prover-loop control: deterministic tactic stepping, stable benchmark behavior, and cleaner replay semantics.

Ralf Stephan said:

What do you think about the possibility of lean-lsp MCP instead of the dojo? (MCP has goal state)

We’re already on that path: in v0.2.1, we support an optional Lean LSP/MCP track (including goal-state/diagnostic loops) for prove --prove-mode llm and formalize, and in TUI you can select it via Settings -> Prover Settings -> LLM mode typecheck backend -> lsp (for prove LLM mode) or Settings -> Prover Settings -> Formalize typecheck backend -> lsp (for formalize); for now Dojo remains the default for tactic-search because replay/cache stability is stronger there, and LSP is only used for LLM/typecheck loops (tactic/lemma search in TUI still runs on Dojo, or mock when no Lean project), while we gate default promotion through parity checks (runner semantics, replay determinism, and non- regression on internal + miniF2F).

UlamAI got a massive update at v.0.2.3 and can now attempt proofs in informal way with output in .tex. After you connect your favorite LLM there's a loop with additional step of "math workers" trying to prove a theorem while "math judges" are checking their work.
